title: Reach sibling commons features only through the layer root

facts.note: Importing module lives inside a commons feature directory commons/<layer>/<feature>/.
Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.

Observer must resolve EVERY import of an in-scope module (pre-existing or newly added/changed) and detect a target inside a different commons feature directory than the importer. Not limited to diff edits.
Detector finding emitted by the validator.

fires: A module under commons/<layer>/<featureA>/ adds an import resolving to a file inside commons/<layer>/<featureB>/ (a sibling feature's internals).
A module under commons/<layer>/<featureA>/ already contains (unchanged) an import resolving into commons/<layer>/<featureB>/ internals.
An existing commons module's import is retargeted from the layer root to a path inside a sibling feature directory.
doesNotFire: A commons feature module imports another feature's capability through the layer root.
A module imports a file inside its own commons feature directory.
A test file or a file in a vendored/build directory imports a sibling feature's internals.
An import uses a bare npm specifier.
The importing file has no layer segment in its path.

given: A module inside a commons feature directory `commons/<layer>/<feature>/…`
when: it imports a capability of a sibling commons feature
then: The import MUST go through the layer root, never directly into the sibling feature's internals.
prefer: Reuse an export that already represents the required capability.
If the capability is intentionally shared, expose the smallest stable surface from the layer root.
If it is not a shared responsibility, keep the implementation local instead of reaching across.
avoid: Importing a path inside a sibling commons feature's directory.
Creating a generic shared module merely to make the import legal.
unless: Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.
A file with no layer segment is outside these rules rather than in violation of them.
why: A feature's internals are its own; the layer root is the surface it deliberately exposes. Reaching past it couples two features through a path neither chose to publish, which is how a shared module quietly becomes unsplittable.
evidence: The cross-feature dependency goes through the intended public boundary (layer root); bun_clean_architecture_detector reports no finding for this rule.
verifier_detail: Resolve each import of a module under commons/<layer>/<feature>/ and flag one whose resolved target sits inside a different commons feature directory.
Term commons_feature: a directory under `commons/<layer>/`, whose internals belong to it alone.
Term layer_root: the surface a feature deliberately exposes; cross-feature use goes through it, or two features are coupled through a path neither published.
Skip test files and vendored/build directories (never scanned).
Do not layer-check bare npm specifiers (they resolve outside the project graph).
Files with no layer segment in their path are out of scope, not violations.

sharedNodes.text: Fix guidance is organised as: During GREEN (rule-specific moves), Do not broaden (rule-specific prohibitions, e.g. do not move unrelated code), Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes.

trace.note: Kept literally as 'strict'; no semantics invented.
